levels.title: Psychology: The Big Picture
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what psychology studies, how psychologists test their ideas and what its main areas are.

levels.title: Who Psychologists Are
levels.objective: After this level you can tell psychologists, psychiatrists and counselors apart and name the main fields psychologists work in.

levels.title: The First Psychology Lab
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what Wilhelm Wundt measured in his 1879 Leipzig lab and why it marks psychology's start as a science.

levels.title: Freud and the Unconscious
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Freud's idea of an unconscious mind and which parts of his theory failed when tested.

levels.title: Behaviorism: Only What You Can See
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why behaviorists like John Watson and B. F. Skinner studied only observable behavior.

levels.title: The Cognitive Revolution
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how psychologists in the 1950s and 1960s began studying the mind as a processor of information.

levels.title: Nature, Nurture or Both?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how twin and adoption studies separate the effects of genes and upbringing.

levels.title: How Psychologists Study People
levels.objective: After this level you can tell apart case studies, surveys, observation and experiments, and what each can and can't show about the mind.

levels.title: Rules That Protect Participants
levels.objective: After this level you can explain informed consent and ethics review boards, and the studies that made them necessary.

levels.title: Checkpoint: What Psychology Is
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how psychology grew from philosophy into a science that tests ideas about the mind.

levels.title: Sensing Versus Perceiving
levels.objective: After this level you can tell sensation from perception and explain how the mind turns raw signals into experience.

levels.title: The Smallest Change You Notice
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the just-noticeable difference and Weber's law.

levels.title: Seeing Wholes, Not Parts
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the Gestalt grouping principles and how they organize what you see.

levels.title: You See What You Expect
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how expectations and context shape perception, called top-down processing.

levels.title: Hearing With Your Eyes
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the McGurk effect and how the mind merges what you see with what you hear.

levels.title: The Cocktail Party Effect
levels.objective: After this level you can explain selective attention and why your own name cuts through a noisy room.

levels.title: The Invisible Gorilla
levels.objective: After this level you can explain inattentional blindness and the basketball study that made it famous.

levels.title: The Multitasking Myth
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why switching between tasks costs time and accuracy.

levels.title: The Subliminal Popcorn Hoax
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what subliminal perception can and cannot do, and why the 1957 movie theater claim was made up.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Perception and Attention
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how perception and attention decide what you notice and what you miss.

levels.title: Pavlov's Dogs
levels.objective: After this level you can explain classical conditioning using Ivan Pavlov's experiments with dogs.

levels.title: Unlearning a Response
levels.objective: After this level you can explain extinction and spontaneous recovery in classical conditioning.

levels.title: Little Albert and Learned Fear
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Watson conditioned fear in an infant and why the study is criticized today.

levels.title: One Bad Meal
levels.objective: After this level you can explain conditioned taste aversion and why it can be learned in a single try.

levels.title: The Skinner Box
levels.objective: After this level you can explain operant conditioning: how consequences change how often a behavior happens.

levels.title: Reinforcement Versus Punishment
levels.objective: After this level you can tell positive and negative reinforcement and punishment apart in everyday examples.

levels.title: Why Slot Machines Hook People
levels.objective: After this level you can explain reinforcement schedules and why unpredictable rewards keep a behavior going longest.

levels.title: Learning by Watching
levels.objective: After this level you can explain observational learning and what Albert Bandura's Bobo doll study showed.

levels.title: How Habits Form
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a cue, a routine and a reward build a habit, and how long habits really take to form.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Learning and Habits
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how association, consequences and watching others shape what we do.

levels.title: Three Stops for a Memory
levels.objective: After this level you can explain sensory, short-term and long-term memory and how information moves between them.

levels.title: Holding Things in Mind
levels.objective: After this level you can explain working memory's small capacity and how chunking stretches it.

levels.title: Knowing That and Knowing How
levels.objective: After this level you can tell explicit memories of facts and events from implicit memories like skills, using patient H.M.'s case.

levels.title: Remembering Where You Learned It
levels.objective: After this level you can explain context-dependent memory and why the famous underwater study gives mixed results today.

levels.title: The Forgetting Curve
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Hermann Ebbinghaus measured forgetting on himself and what shape the curve takes.

levels.title: Study Tricks That Work
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the spacing and testing effects and why rereading works less well than it feels.

levels.title: Memory Rebuilds the Past
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why remembering is reconstruction, using Frederic Bartlett's "War of the Ghosts" study.

levels.title: Memories That Never Happened
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Elizabeth Loftus showed that leading questions and suggestion can create false memories.

levels.title: When Eyewitnesses Get It Wrong
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why confident eyewitnesses can pick the wrong person and how lineups are made fairer.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Memory
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how memories are stored, strengthened and rebuilt, and why they can mislead.

levels.title: What Gets You Moving
levels.objective: After this level you can explain drives, homeostasis and incentives as sources of motivation.

levels.title: Maslow's Pyramid
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Maslow's hierarchy of needs and what later research changed about it.

levels.title: When Rewards Backfire
levels.objective: After this level you can explain intrinsic and extrinsic motivation and how rewards can undermine interest.

levels.title: Willpower as a Battery?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the ego depletion theory and why large replication attempts failed to confirm it.

levels.title: What an Emotion Is
levels.objective: After this level you can compare the James-Lange, Cannon-Bard and two-factor theories of emotion.

levels.title: Are Facial Expressions Universal?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Paul Ekman's evidence for universal expressions and the current debate over it.

levels.title: Does Smiling Make You Happier?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the facial feedback idea and why its replication record is mixed.

levels.title: The Sleep-Deprived Mind
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how losing sleep affects mood, attention and judgment.

levels.title: What Dreams Say About You
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what research on dream content shows and how it compares with Freud's dream interpretation.

levels.title: Milestone: Inside the Mind
levels.objective: After this level you can connect perception, learning, memory, motivation and emotion into one picture of how experience becomes action.

levels.title: Fast Thinking, Slow Thinking
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the two-systems idea of fast intuition and slow deliberation, and when each takes over.

levels.title: If It Comes to Mind, It Seems Common
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the availability heuristic and why dramatic risks feel more likely than they are.

levels.title: The First Number Wins
levels.objective: After this level you can explain anchoring, using the experiment with a rigged wheel of fortune.

levels.title: The Linda Problem
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the representativeness heuristic and how a good story can beat the odds in our judgment.

levels.title: The Halo Effect
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the halo effect: how one good trait colors our judgment of everything else about a person.

levels.title: Testing Only What You Believe
levels.objective: After this level you can explain confirmation bias using Peter Wason's 2-4-6 number puzzle.

levels.title: I Knew It All Along
levels.objective: After this level you can explain hindsight bias and how researchers caught people rewriting their own predictions.

levels.title: Overconfidence and Dunning-Kruger
levels.objective: After this level you can explain overconfidence research and why the Dunning-Kruger effect is debated.

levels.title: Priming: A Famous Finding Falls
levels.objective: After this level you can explain which priming effects hold up and why the "slow walking" priming study failed to replicate.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Mental Shortcuts
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why the mind uses shortcuts and how the research showed where they go wrong.

levels.title: Comfort Over Food
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what Harry Harlow's monkey studies showed about attachment and why they are ethically criticized.

levels.title: Secure and Insecure Attachment
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Mary Ainsworth's Strange Situation and the attachment styles it describes.

levels.title: Piaget's Stages
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Jean Piaget's stages of thinking and where later research found children more capable.

levels.title: Knowing Others Have Minds
levels.objective: After this level you can explain theory of mind and the false-belief test used to show when children develop it.

levels.title: How Babies Crack Language
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how infants pick out words and why language is easiest to learn early.

levels.title: The Marshmallow Test
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the delay-of-gratification studies and what a 2018 replication changed about their meaning.

levels.title: Why Teens Take More Risks
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the presence of peers raises teenagers' risk taking in experiments.

levels.title: Erikson's Life Stages
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Erik Erikson's stages of development from infancy to old age.

levels.title: Older and Happier?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain which mental abilities fade with age, which grow, and why older adults often report more contentment.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Growing Up and Growing Old
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how minds change from infancy to old age and which classic findings held up.

levels.title: Asch's Lines
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Solomon Asch's conformity experiments and what made people more or less likely to go along.

levels.title: Milgram's Shock Machine
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Stanley Milgram's obedience studies, their main criticisms and later partial replications.

levels.title: The Stanford Prison Experiment
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what the 1971 study claimed and why critics say it does not show what it claimed.

levels.title: Why Bystanders Hesitate
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the bystander effect and why the famous story of 38 silent witnesses was wrong.

levels.title: Blaming the Person, Not the Situation
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the fundamental attribution error and the experiment that first showed it.

levels.title: Changing Your Mind to Fit Your Actions
levels.objective: After this level you can explain cognitive dissonance using Leon Festinger's one-dollar experiment.

levels.title: Two Roads to Persuasion
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the central and peripheral routes to persuasion and when each one works.

levels.title: Us Versus Them
levels.objective: After this level you can explain in-group favoritism and how the minimal group studies produced it from almost nothing.

levels.title: Culture and the WEIRD Problem
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how culture shapes thinking and why findings from WEIRD samples may not apply everywhere.

levels.title: Checkpoint: The Social Animal
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how other people shape what we believe and do, and which famous studies need caution.

levels.title: The Big Five
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the five personality traits psychologists measure and what each one describes.

levels.title: What's Wrong With Personality Types
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why type tests like the Myers-Briggs score poorly on reliability compared with trait measures.

levels.title: Does Personality Change?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how stable personality is across a lifetime and how it tends to mature.

levels.title: What IQ Tests Measure
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what IQ tests measure, what scores predict, and why average scores rose over the 20th century.

levels.title: Stress Lives in the Appraisal
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the way you judge a demand and your resources shapes how stressful it feels.

levels.title: Coping That Helps
levels.objective: After this level you can compare problem-focused and emotion-focused coping and judge which fits a given situation.

levels.title: Bouncing Back
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what research on loss and hardship shows about how common resilience is.

levels.title: What Happiness Research Finds
levels.objective: After this level you can explain hedonic adaptation and why relationships predict wellbeing better than windfalls.

levels.title: Changing a Habit
levels.objective: After this level you can apply cues, rewards and if-then plans to change a real habit.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Personality and Wellbeing
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how traits, appraisals and habits shape how people cope and thrive.

levels.title: What Counts as a Mental Disorder
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how clinicians distinguish a mental disorder from ordinary struggles and what the DSM is.

levels.title: When Worry Won't Switch Off
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how everyday anxiety differs from an anxiety disorder such as panic disorder or a phobia.

levels.title: Understanding Depression
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how depression differs from sadness and why no single cause, such as a chemical imbalance, explains it.

levels.title: Beyond Anxiety and Depression
levels.objective: After this level you can explain in general terms what ADHD, OCD, PTSD and bipolar disorder are, and why casual labels mislead.

levels.title: How Talk Therapy Works
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what cognitive behavioral therapy does and what research says about how well therapy works.

levels.title: Talking About Mental Health
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how to talk about mental health without stigma and where to point someone who needs help.

levels.title: The Replication Crisis
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why many psychology findings failed to replicate and what psychologists changed as a result.

levels.title: Power Posing: Rise and Fall
levels.objective: After this level you can trace how the power posing finding spread and weigh what replications later showed.

levels.title: Spotting Psychology Myths
levels.objective: After this level you can weigh popular claims, like learning styles and venting anger, against the research evidence.

levels.title: Mastery Challenge: Psychology
levels.objective: After this level you can demonstrate command of Psychology Levels 1 to 99 across the whole tree.
